title: Quantum-Enhanced Inference of Conditional Future Probabilities with Reduced Memory Cost
authors: Jianjun Chen, Akshat Gupta, Chengran Yang, Ariel Neufeld, Jayne Thompson, Thomas J. Elliott, Mile Gu
abstract: Many potential future events have devastating consequences, from the onset of earthquakes to financial black swan events. Accurate predictions of their probability of occurrence are vital. Yet as the stochastic systems underlying such events become increasingly complex, these probabilities can depend on ever-growing amounts of past data, which require ever more memory to track. The accuracy of our estimates is ultimately limited by both computational and memory constraints; the former to reduce sampling error, the latter to avoid sampling bias. Traditional quantum algorithms -- such as amplitude estimation -- address only the former, and become untenable especially in near-future quantum devices where quantum memory is a premium. Here, we offer quantum-algorithmic means to reduce systematic bias while maintaining a quadratic speed-up. Our results thus advance the timeline for the practical deployment of quantum technologies, and illustrate their additional benefits when simulating processes of growing complexity.
summary: This paper introduces a quantum-algorithmic framework to estimate the probability of future events in complex stochastic systems. It tackles the fundamental trade-off between memory requirements and estimation accuracy by combining quantum amplitude estimation with quantum-enhanced dimensional reduction. The results demonstrate that quantum methods can maintain high accuracy while drastically reducing the memory overhead compared to classical methods.
main_problem: The core challenge is accurately estimating the conditional probability of a future event in complex stochastic systems while overcoming the exponential memory scaling and computational limitations of traditional quantum algorithms.
main_result: The authors propose a quantum-algorithmic method that simultaneously achieves a quadratic speed-up (like QAE) and significantly reduces the systematic bias associated with memory constraints.
method: The approach involves mapping classical stochastic processes to quantum memory states and employing a structured quantum circuit (MRQPE) to estimate probabilities, incorporating quantum-enhanced dimensional reduction techniques.
model_or_system: The work analyzes stationary stochastic processes, including Autoregressive (AR(2)) models and cyclic random walks, which are discretized and modeled using quantum memory registers.
key_observables: Conditional future probabilities $P(X_{0:L} | \leftarrow x)$, estimation error ($\epsilon$), and the fidelity divergence rate (QFDR).
important_parameters: Memory dimension ($D_c$ vs. $	ilde{D}$), required number of simulations ($N$), and the time horizon ($L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating the full quantum model with a reduced memory dimension ($	ilde{D} < D_c$) while maintaining low estimation error.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the unitary evolution coupling memory and ancilla, the structured quantum circuit for state preparation, and comparisons of mean absolute errors for various time series models (AR(2), coin process) under noise.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of memory vs. accuracy trade-off, then details the quantum-algorithmic framework (MRQPE) for state preparation, and finally validates the method by applying it to various time series models (AR(2), Poisson processes) to demonstrate simultaneous reduction in bias and memory cost.
why_interesting: It directly addresses the practical limitations of quantum computation for simulating complex, long-term physical processes by showing how quantum techniques can manage the exponential growth of required classical memory states.
